title: Nora Fatehi Walked Onto a World Cup Stage in Toronto and Became the Most Googled Bollywood Star on Earth
excerpt: In a red ensemble, flanked by hundreds of dancers, she performed the official FIFA anthem 'Siir Siir' before Canada's match — and outpaced Priyanka, Deepika and Alia in global searches overnight. Twice now, the World Cup has belonged to her.
body:
The pitch at BMO Field was drowned in the red of the Canadian flag, gold scattered across it like confetti, and then she arrived — Nora Fatehi, in a red ensemble, walking out to headline the second opening ceremony of the FIFA World Cup 2026 as a global audience held its breath.

This is the woman who once entered Bollywood as a contestant on Bigg Boss. On June 12, she opened football's biggest tournament. And by the time the broadcast cut away, she had done something no other Indian entertainer managed all week: she became the most Googled Bollywood artist in the world, outpacing Priyanka Chopra, Deepika Padukone and Alia Bhatt in a single night, according to Google Trends.

The performance itself was pure spectacle. Nora took the stage alongside French singer Vegedream and producer DJ Sanjoy to perform 'Siir Siir,' one of the official anthems of the 2026 World Cup — a track inspired, fittingly, by a chant Moroccan fans turned into folklore during the 2022 tournament in Qatar. Hundreds of dancers moved with her. Her vocals were live, her choreography was relentless, and the crowd, as one report put it, simply erupted.

https://www.instagram.com/reel/DZeZbc7suBD/
**""This journey of mine has been an incredible roller coaster ride."

It is, remarkably, her second World Cup."**

"Canada gave me the base, Morocco gave me the roots and India gave me the wings to fly!" — Nora Fatehi

That line, posted to her Instagram alongside a string of images from the stage, is the whole story in one sentence. Nora was raised in Toronto. Her heritage is Moroccan. Her stardom was built in India. So when she stood at the centre of a World Cup ceremony in the very city that raised her, performing an anthem rooted in Moroccan football culture, every thread of her improbable identity came together on one stage. "What a magical moment," she wrote. "This journey of mine has been an incredible roller coaster ride."

It is, remarkably, her second World Cup. She delivered a memorable showcase during the 2022 celebrations, which makes her one of the very few performers — of any nationality — invited back to football's grandest platform twice. "It's such a privilege to be able to say that I got the opportunity to perform at the FIFA World Cup twice," she said. The repeat booking is its own quiet verdict: the organisers didn't just want a Bollywood name for novelty. They wanted her, specifically, because she delivers.

What makes Nora magnetic on a stage like this is that she refuses to be only one thing. She is a singer and a dancer in the same breath, switching between live vocals and the kind of choreography that built her legend on tracks like 'Dilbar' and 'Saki Saki.' Most performers anchor to one craft. Nora runs both at full throttle, and on a 360-degree stadium stage that ability is what separates a viral moment from a forgettable one.

The diaspora felt every second of it. For Indian football fans — long starved of representation on the sport's biggest night — watching a desi star headline the ceremony was a genuine point of pride. The image travelled instantly: Nora in red, the Canadian gold behind her, an Indian flag's worth of cultural weight on her shoulders. She'd already set the tone earlier, carrying the Moroccan flag and singing the anthem ahead of the Morocco–Brazil opener, a draw she watched from the stands like the football obsessive she genuinely is.

For those who want to relive it, the FIFA World Cup 2026 broadcasts across the US on Fox Sports and stream on Peacock Premium and Fubo TV, with the opening ceremony segments widely circulating online — and Nora has been generous with behind-the-scenes glimpses on her own Instagram. 'Siir Siir' is streaming on Spotify, where she's been actively pushing fans to listen.

There's a tendency to underestimate Nora Fatehi — to file her under "item number" and move on. This week should retire that instinct for good. She stood on the world's largest stage, in front of a billion-eyed audience, and walked off as the most searched Bollywood star on the planet. Not because of a film, not because of a controversy, but because she performed. The tournament runs through July 19, and the football will, rightly, take over the headlines. But the opening belonged to a girl from Toronto with Moroccan roots and Indian wings — and she did not waste a single second of it.
